BoardMeetsWhat it can do
MarchOpens the second Monday of MarchVerifies the current year's roll and hears appeals
JulyMay meet the Tuesday after the third Monday in JulyCorrects qualified errors for the current and one prior year
DecemberMay meet the Tuesday after the second Monday in DecemberMakes the same qualified error corrections

The City of Saginaw notes that July and December boards sit only when there are errors to correct or poverty exemptions to weigh, and that every board can rule on poverty exemption applications for the current year. Each local unit sets its own schedule, so check with your assessor before assuming a date.

What happens when Saginaw County taxes go delinquent?

Past-due real property tax is payable at the counter, by mail or on the web. Counter payments can be cash, money order or certified check, while personal checks work only for first-year delinquencies before January 1. Visa, MasterCard and Discover are taken, and the mailing address is Saginaw County Treasurer, 111 S. Michigan Avenue, Saginaw, MI 48602.

The web option runs at all hours through a vendor, which charges an access fee on the whole payment. The card policy contains these rules:

  • A photo ID issued by a government must accompany a card payment, and the card must carry the payer's name.
  • If a payment is reversed or declined, it is treated as void and all fees, interest and forfeiture fees reapply from the original date.
  • A voided payment that had a redemption certificate recorded adds $20 for the correction.
  • An overpayment below $3 is absorbed into interest, and larger refunds return to the same card.
  • Payments post to the parcel you name, with no refund for paying the wrong parcel.

The county was also a defendant in Fox v. Saginaw County, a federal class action settled over surplus money from tax foreclosure auctions between 2013 and 2020. Claims closed on July 16, 2026.

Does selling reset the tax bill in Saginaw County?

Some transfers do not count as a change of ownership, including a transfer between spouses, a residential transfer to a close relative such as a parent, child or grandchild with no commercial use afterward, and certain trust and foreclosure transfers.

A warranty deed arriving at the register also needs the Treasurer's certificate, priced at $5 for the first five descriptions and $1 per extra description. State law ties it to proof that the preceding five years of taxes are paid (MCL 211.135). Quitclaim deeds without a warranty are excepted. Request a written payoff from the Treasurer before choosing a closing date if any year is delinquent.

How big is the Saginaw County housing stock?

Saginaw County covers 816 square miles in Mid-Michigan, drained by rivers that join into the Saginaw River. The 2020 census recorded 190,124 residents in 78,442 households and 85,953 housing units, 8.7% of them empty. Owners held 70.5% of occupied homes. Single-person households made up roughly a third of the total, and the median age was 41.3.

The cities are Saginaw, Frankenmuth and Zilwaukee, and the rest is townships such as Birch Run, Chesaning, Kochville and Swan Creek. I-75 and I-675 serve the metro area, and US 23 plus M-13, M-46 and M-47 fill in the grid. MBS International Airport sits near Freeland.

A parcel's school district changes the bill. Districts include Saginaw Public Schools, Saginaw Township Community Schools, Frankenmuth, Chesaning Union, Birch Run Area, Freeland Community, Hemlock Public, Swan Valley and Bridgeport-Spaulding. Saginaw Valley State University and Delta College anchor higher education.

How old is the Saginaw County tax base?

The county was created by September 10, 1822 and fully organized on February 9, 1835. Sawmills and farms were spreading along the river by the early 1850s, and the Michigan historical markers in the county include the Saginaw Valley lumbering era, Saginaw oil industry and Saginaw Valley coal. The county today holds a mix of platted city lots, rural townships and riverfront land, each assessed by a different local office.

The county parks commission runs six parks covering more than 550 acres. Every other parcel, from a Frankenmuth storefront to a farm in Brant Township, is billed by the local unit where it lies and collected by the County Treasurer if it goes unpaid.

The Treasurer and the Register of Deeds both work from the same courthouse on S. Michigan Avenue, so one trip can cover a certificate and the filing.

Your city or township treasurer mails it. Delinquent real property tax moves to the County Treasurer at (989) 790-5225.

When do Saginaw County appeals open each year?

Local boards open on the second Monday of March and keep sessions through that week. Your local assessor's office posts the exact schedule.

Yes. The County Treasurer accepts web payments at any hour through an outside vendor, for an access fee. Card payments at the counter require the named payer's government photo ID.

It can. Taxable value resets to state equalized value the next year, and the buyer reports the transfer inside 45 days.

Which office sends the bill and which collects late tax?

Each city and township in Wayne County prepares its own assessment and tax rolls and mails July and December bills from its own treasurer. The county treasurer steps in only for delinquent real property, at 400 Monroe Street, 5th Floor, in Detroit.

A separate unit, the Assessment and Equalization Division of the Department of Management and Budget at 500 Griswold, Suite 2650, advises the County Commission on equalizing local values and apportioning taxes. Call (313) 967-0010 or write equalization@waynecountymi.gov for the Parcel Viewer GIS app. The division also offers annual assessment data, historical GIS parcel shape files and old tax maps for download at no cost. Detroit has its own assessor at (313) 224-3035 and a City Treasurer property tax division at (313) 224-3560.

For a current bill, anywhere in the county, start with the treasurer of the city or township where the house stands.

When tax becomes delinquent

The cutoff is the end of February. Tax not paid to the local treasurer by then turns delinquent on March 1, and only the Wayne County Treasurer takes payment afterward. The county takes part in the Delinquent Tax Revolving Fund program, and every community and school district is in it. Detroit joined starting with tax year 2003.

The county's tax information line is (313) 224-5990. Delinquent accounts can be settled several ways:

  • Online with a bank debit, which costs nothing.
  • Online with Visa, MasterCard or American Express, which adds a 2.49 percent fee paid to the processor.
  • A partial payment by mail or in person, with a stamped, self-addressed envelope if you want a receipt.

County staff have no authority to waive penalties and interest or to shrink a bill after it is issued, because the state expects each taxpayer to pay on time. Cutting future bills is a job for exemptions, which the local assessor decides.

Forfeiture and foreclosure timeline

Public Act 123 of 1999, codified at MCL 211.78, shortened the road to tax foreclosure from roughly five years to roughly two. The table condenses the stages.

Stages of tax forfeiture and foreclosure for Wayne County parcels

First March 1 after the bill yearUnpaid taxes are delinquent and go to the county treasurer, with a 4% administration fee and 1% interest per month

Before any foreclosure, the treasurer reports at least ten contacts: four first class letters, three certified ones, a personal visit and two occupant mailings.

What relief can the Treasurer offer before foreclosure?

Payment plans and a hardship extension are the two main tools. The extension is open to owners who hold title by recorded deed or land contract, occupy the home as a principal residence and face a substantial financial hardship. The income yardstick is 125 percent of the federal income guideline, but owners slightly above it are told to apply anyway.

  • Bring photo ID from Michigan, the deed, proof you live there such as a utility bill, and proof of income.
  • The Taxpayer Assistance staff reply within 30 days once the application is complete.
  • Applications come from the treasurer's page, by phone at (313) 224-5990, or at the office by appointment.
  • Title trouble can go to United Community Housing Coalition, (313) 963-3310, or the Legal Aid and Defender Association, (313) 964-4130.

A hardship exemption that can trim or erase future bills is requested through the local assessing unit. Lenders sometimes miss tax payments after a refinance, so match your mortgage statements against the local treasurer's records.

Selling a Wayne County house with tax owing

You can sell, provided the tax is paid by closing. A warranty deed has to carry county treasurer certificates reporting no tax liens and five prior years of paid taxes, under MCL 211.135, while a quitclaim without warranty covenants is excused.

For deed certification the county treasurer charges $5.00 per document covering up to 25 parcel numbers, plus 20 cents for each additional parcel. Only originals qualify. Mail them with a check or money order to Wayne County Treasurer, Deed Certification, 400 Monroe St., 5th Floor, Detroit, MI 48226, enclosing a stamped return envelope, or bring them to an appointment. The certified deed then goes to the Register of Deeds, which requires its own appointment for recording.

When a parcel is already forfeited, payment remains possible until the following March, and interest keeps building monthly. Paying off the balance from sale proceeds beats waiting for foreclosure. A cash buyer can close on a short timeline, so ask for the county payoff early and let the title company settle it at the table.

Appeals and county equalization

Appeals start locally, at the city or township Board of Review and then the Michigan Tax Tribunal. If either one changed your value, ask the local assessor's office or the Tribunal for an explanation.

Equalization is a second look at the totals. Under MCL 211.30a, every local unit delivers its roll to the county equalization division by the Wednesday following the first Monday in April. The Board of Commissioners convenes the Tuesday after the second Monday in April and must finish by the first Monday in May under MCL 211.34. The aim is to spread the countywide tax burden evenly among cities and townships.

What happens to a foreclosed property?

State and local governments get first refusal on a foreclosed parcel at the minimum bid. Whatever they pass over goes to public auction in September and October of the foreclosure year, opening at the delinquent taxes, penalties and interest. Winners receive a quit claim deed, and every sale is "as is" and "where is".

Former owners may still recover leftover money. MCL 211.78t lets a person who held title or equity at foreclosure claim any proceeds above the debt, starting with a notarized notice of intent delivered by July 1 after the foreclosure. The treasurer answers by January 31, and a circuit court motion can follow between February 1 and May 15.

Wayne County housing at a glance

Wayne County is the most populous in Michigan, with Detroit as the seat. Dearborn, Livonia, Westland, Taylor, Wyandotte and the Grosse Pointes are also here, and the southern communities are called Downriver. About 64.8 percent of homes are owner-occupied, the median home value is $178,500 and median rent is $1,132. Values vary by community, so the local assessor's record carries more weight than a countywide figure.

Frequently asked questions

When do Wayne County property taxes go delinquent?

March 1. Tax not paid to the local city or township treasurer by the end of February is delinquent from the next March 1 and can be paid only at the Wayne County Treasurer's Office.

How long before Wayne County can foreclose for unpaid taxes?

About two years. One year of delinquency leads to forfeiture the next March 1, and foreclosure follows a year later unless taxes, interest and fees are paid by the March 31 deadline.

Can the Wayne County Treasurer reduce my tax bill?

No. Once taxes are billed the county cannot reduce them or waive interest and fees. Exemptions that lower future bills are requested from your local assessing unit.

What does Wayne County charge to certify a deed for taxes?

$5.00 per document covering up to 25 parcel numbers, plus 20 cents per added parcel. Only original documents can be certified.

Can I get money back if my Wayne County home sold at foreclosure auction?

Possibly. Owners with title or equity at foreclosure may file a notarized notice of intent to claim surplus proceeds by July 1 after the foreclosure. A court motion follows only if proceeds remain.
